description: Brings the six artifacts of the reference human run H1 in line with the current churn scenario, and corrects one arithmetic slip, for the round-5 regeneration of the showcase.

H1 was recorded before scenario commit ccb537a, which raised the quarterly budget from S$180,000 to S$540,000 (6,000 offers a month at S$30 is S$180,000 a month, so S$540,000 a quarter) and moved the mediation outage that removed about 4% of usage values from March to May.
The recorded modelling and final reports also cost a month of 6,000 offers at S$18,000, which is S$180,000 at S$30 an offer, and derive about S$72 per save from it (S$720 at 250 saves).
Nothing else changes: the analysis content (row counts, rates, model results, runbook) is kept as recorded.

Other scenario facts were checked against the recording and need no change: 480,000 postpaid subscribers, churn from 1.4% to 2.1%, about 6,000 offers a month, S$30 per offer, the 6-month save rule, prepaid out of scope, the churn label including involuntary disconnections, total_charges as text with blanks for new joiners, the June observation month with a monthly refresh, 8,170 rows with 170 repeated subscriber_ids, 635 blank total_charges and 327 rows without usage (the committed extract gives the same counts), the offer levers, and 300 calls a day across a team of four.
The 19 learner messages name no budget figure, no outage month and no offer cost total, so no entry targets a message.
